commands_raw:
In [color=green][b]Genome Garden[/b][/color] all living things are defined by genes makeup that defines everything about them, just like in real life.
---
We've given these genes are given names based on the primary effects they have on the plant e.g. [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code] or [code][b]pigment[/b][/code].
---
In the case of the [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code] gene we've discovered the [color=red][b]R[/b][/color] allele which appears to be responsible for creating a red color!
---
signal(show_red_tulip)
In each flower, each gene is made up of two alleles. This tulip for example has two [color=red][b]R[/b][/color] alleles for it's [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code] gene. Hover over it to take a look!
name: Tutorial_start

commands_raw:
signal(skip_text_animation)
In each flower, each gene is made up of two alleles. This tulip for example has two [color=red][b]R[/b][/color] alleles for it's [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code] gene. Hover over it to take a look!
---
signal(show_yellow_tulip)
When we cross-breed flowers together the child inherits one allele from each parent for each gene. Here's another tulip with [color=GOLD][code]Y[/code][/color] alleles for the [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code] gene. The [color=GOLD][b]Y[/b][/color] allele is responsible or producing a [color=GOLD]yellow[/color] colour! 

[b]Take a look at the Yellow flower[/b]
name: on_red_tulip_hover

commands_raw:
signal(skip_text_animation)
When we cross-breed flowers together the child inherits one allele from each parent for each gene. Here's another tulip with [color=GOLD][code]Y[/code][/color] alleles for the [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code] gene. The [color=GOLD][b]Y[/b][/color] allele is responsible or producing a [color=GOLD]yellow[/color] colour! 

[b]Take a look at the Yellow flower[/b]
---
signal(show_breeder)
signal(set_state_step,breeding_orange)
When we cross-breed two flowers together each child inherits one allele from each parent for each gene. 
Let's try breeding them together and see what happens!
name: on_yellow_tulip_hover

commands_raw:
Woah! An [color=orange]Orange[/color] flower. Different alleles can interact with each other in different ways. The [color=red][b]R[/b][/color] allele and [color=gold][b]Y[/b][/color] [b][i]allele[/i][/b] in this case are said to be [b][i]Codominant[/i][/b] meaning that both [b][i]alleles[/i][/b] can be expressed at the same time.
---
signal(set_state_step,breeding_rb)
signal(show_blue_tulip)
signal(hide_yellow_tulip)
Here's another flower from our nursery. This one has two coppies of the [color=royal_blue][b]b[/b][/color] allele. We've had some interesting results breeding this one. 

[b]Why don't you try cross breeding a [color=royal_blue]blue[/color] and [color=red]red[/color] flower.[/b]

[b]You can uproot plants by right clicking on them to make room for new ones.[/b]
name: on_orange_flower_bred

commands_raw:
Huh. Looks like were only getting [color=red]red[/color] children? Let me take a closer look at them...
---
They're all getting a [color=red]R[/color] from the [color=red]red[/color] flower and a [color=royal_blue]b[/color] from the [color=royal_blue]blue[/color], that is they have [code][b]colour_1[/b][/code]: [color=red]R[/color][color=royal_blue]b[/color]. Looks like the [color=red]red[/color] [i]allele's[/i] effect is [i]dominant[/i] over the [color=royal_blue]blue[/color].
---
Since these children all have the [color=royal_blue]blue[/color] gene let's see if we can get a pure blue ([colour=royal_blue]bb[/colour]) child.
name: on_third_rb_flower

commands_raw:
We're trying to breed a [color=brickred]Red[/color] flower with a [color=gold]Yellow[/color] flower at the moment. 

[b]You can right click to uproot a flower and discard it.[/b]
name: on_same_parent_orange_breed

commands_raw:
We're trying to breed a [color=brickred]Red[/color] flower with a [color=Blue]Blue[/color] flower at the moment. 

[b]You can right click to uproot a flower and discard it.[/b]
name: on_same_parent_rb_breed

commands_raw:
Since these children all have the [color=royal_blue]blue[/color] gene let's see if we can get a pure blue ([colour=royal_blue]bb[/colour]) child.
---
It took a couple of tries but there it is! That blue flower managed to inherit the [color=royal_blue]b[/color] allele from the right and the [color=royal_blue]blue[/color] from the left parent.

Let me show you a couple of tools we use to help us better understand how genes are transfered from the parents to the children.
---
signal(show_predictor)
This is the [b]Predictor[/b]. It's a little slow but it's able to compute all possible visually distinct children tht could come from two parents. It's even able to tell you what percentage of the time you should expect to see each child!
---
signal(show_yellow_tulip)
signal(set_state,orange_predictor)
Here's the yellow flower back, why don't you breed a couple more orange flowers and use two of them as a test for the predictor.
name: on_blue_flower_bred

commands_raw:
